effects.title: Hello
effects.summary: The smallest effect: a few hundred stars drifting slowly across a dark field, one instanced draw through the HDR tail. Each star is a naive fixed disc, the baseline the energy-conserving star spot is measured against. Every later effect starts from this shape.

scorecard.fallback: A still of the stars, or box-shadow stars in CSS.
useCases: The template for new effects

effects.title: Deep field
effects.summary: A starfield that never shimmers, over a flat nebula: four depth layers of stars from the sky's own magnitudes and colours, drifting slowly and shifting with the pointer and the page's scroll, in front of hydrogen-red and oxygen-teal gas crossed by dust lanes. Every star keeps its light wherever it sits between pixels; the nebula is drawn once and only moved.

scorecard.fallback: A still of the field, or box-shadow stars in CSS over a gradient.
useCases: A space hero behind a headline
A launch or science page background

effects.title: Real sky
effects.summary: The sky above you tonight: the 9 096 stars of the Yale Bright Star Catalogue where they are for your time zone's city at this moment, with the planets among them, turning in a gentle time-lapse over a dark skyline. Each star's altitude comes from the sidereal time and your latitude on the GPU; low stars are dimmed by the air and twinkle harder and faster, and bright ones flash colours, as they do near the horizon.

scorecard.fallback: A still of tonight’s sky, drawn once on the server or as a poster.
useCases: "The sky above you tonight" on an astronomy or travel page
A night-sky hero that is true to the visitor’s place

effects.title: Star splat
effects.summary: The family's building block, laid out: stars as points with a temperature and a magnitude. A row from 2 400 K to 40 000 K, coloured by Planck's law; a row of magnitudes 0 to 6, a hundred times dimmer at the end; diffraction spikes as a Hubble or a JWST image draws them; over a drifting field drawn from the sky's own statistics. Every star is a Gaussian integrated over each pixel, so it keeps its light and its look wherever it sits.

scorecard.fallback: A still of the rows and the field.
useCases: A reference for star colour and brightness
The spot every space effect draws

effects.title: Star trails
effects.summary: A long exposure facing the celestial pole: every star sweeps an arc of 15° an hour round it, coloured by its temperature, over a dark skyline. The exposure grows over forty seconds to an hour and three quarters of sky, holds, and starts again. Drawn in closed form, each arc at its current length, so nothing accumulates and nothing is lost on a resize.

scorecard.fallback: A still of the full exposure.
useCases: A slow, calm night hero
An astronomy or photography page

effects.title: Data galaxy
effects.summary: A page's own data drawn as a galaxy: every point a star, every cluster an arm in its own colour, every value a brightness, turning slowly. Point at a star to pick it: it lights up, its cluster brightens round it, and the canvas fires an `sr-pick` event with the point's label and value for the page to show.

scorecard.fallback: A still of the galaxy, or the data as a plain chart.
useCases: A product page: "our community"
An embedding or clustering, explored by hover

effects.title: Galaxy collision
effects.summary: Two disc galaxies passing each other on a parabolic orbit, as Toomre and Toomre showed in 1972: each a massive core with 12 000 stars round it, which feel both cores' gravity, so the close pass throws out long tidal tails and a bridge between them. Integrated in compute, sub-step by sub-step, over a minute's passage; then it begins again.

scorecard.fallback: A still of the tails at their longest.
useCases: A science showpiece
A "merging" or "two worlds" hero

effects.title: Nebula
effects.summary: An emission nebula in three layers, coloured by the lines its gas glows in: hydrogen-alpha red, oxygen teal where the gas is hottest, sulphur at its edges, as the eye sees them or in the Hubble palette. The layers move apart with the pointer and scroll, stars sit between them, and the near layer is dark dust that hides the stars and glow behind it. Each layer is drawn once and only moved.

useCases: A space hero behind a headline
A science or astronomy page background

effects.title: Nebula volume
effects.summary: An emission nebula as a volume, turning slowly: a ray march through 3D noise, its gas glowing in sulphur, hydrogen and oxygen lines brightest near the hot stars inside it, its dust lanes absorbing the glow and the stars behind. Marched at half resolution with jitter averaged over frames, on Fire Temple’s emission-absorption kernel.

scorecard.fallback: A still of the nebula, or the flat nebula.
useCases: A science showpiece
A slow, deep hero background

effects.title: Spiral galaxy
effects.summary: A spiral galaxy by the density wave: every star on an ellipse whose orientation turns with its size, so the ellipses crowd into two arms that keep their shape while every star moves through them. A golden bulge, blue young stars and pink H II regions along the arms, dust lanes just inside them, and a dozen tracer stars to watch the stars outrun the arms.

useCases: A science or space hero
A "data as a galaxy" starting point

effects.title: Black hole
effects.summary: A black hole with a glowing accretion disc, every ray traced through Schwarzschild's metric: the disc's far side bent up over the top and under the bottom, the thin photon ring, the shadow. The side of the disc coming towards you is Doppler-brightened and bluer, the inner edge dimmed by gravitational redshift, and the starfield behind is lensed round it, after the hole in Interstellar.

scorecard.fallback: A still of the hole, or the thin-lens cursor.
useCases: A science showpiece
A dramatic hero for a launch or a talk

effects.title: Lens cursor
effects.summary: The pointer as a small black hole: a gravitational lens that bends whatever is behind it into an Einstein ring, with a second, flipped image inside, a black shadow and its faint photon ring. One pass, by the thin-lens equation, over a nebula the effect draws or an image the page hands over.

useCases: A cursor for a science or space page
A hover over a hero image

effects.title: Orbits
effects.summary: The solar system today, from JPL's published orbital elements: every planet where it is on this date, moving at a few days a second along its orbit. Distances on a logarithmic scale, so Mercury and Neptune both fit, and scrolling the page zooms in on the inner planets.

scorecard.fallback: A still of the planets today.
useCases: An astronomy or education page
A "where are the planets now" widget

effects.title: Gas giant
effects.summary: Jupiter, Saturn or Neptune: belts and zones between alternating jets, their clouds carried along by the winds so they shear into streaks and curls, storms like the Great Red Spot that persist and drift with their bands, limb darkening, and Saturn's rings from their real optical depths, with the planet's shadow across them and theirs across it.

useCases: A hero for a science or space page
A slow, living backdrop behind a title

effects.title: Moon phase
effects.summary: The Moon as a progress indicator: its phase is the value, mapped so the lit area grows evenly, with a soft terminator a loader can sweep, craters the low sun picks out along it, Moon Temple's maria and Lommel-Seeliger face, and earthshine on the dark side, bluish and strongest in a thin crescent.

scorecard.fallback: A half disc and a scaled ellipse in CSS, which draw the exact shape of the light; two offset circles do not.
useCases: A loader or progress indicator
A date widget: tonight’s Moon

effects.title: Planet
effects.summary: An Earthlike world from orbit, every pixel a ray: continents and mountains on a cube map with no seams, oceans that catch the sun, clouds with their shadows on the ground, city lights past the terminator, and blue air scattered at the limb and reddened at dusk. Scrolling the page turns it from day to night.

scorecard.fallback: A still of the planet half lit.
useCases: A hero for a space, climate or geography page that turns from day to night on scroll
A sky at sunset, from the same atmosphere, behind a landing page

effects.title: Total eclipse
effects.summary: A total solar eclipse as a countdown: the Moon slides over the Sun, the last of the photosphere breaks into Baily's beads through the valleys on the Moon's limb, the diamond ring flares, and the corona, a millionth of the disc's brightness, comes out with the pink chromosphere and prominences as the eye's exposure follows the light.

useCases: A launch countdown to a date
A hero for an eclipse or astronomy page

effects.title: Solar surface
effects.summary: The Sun in white light: granulation as convection cells that rise and fade, sunspots with dark umbrae and filamentary penumbrae, faculae near the limb, and limb darkening from the physics, every pixel a blackbody at the temperature we see into there. Prominences and the corona beyond the limb, as a coronagraph would show them.

useCases: A hero for a solar, energy or science page
A warm, slowly churning backdrop
